run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T08:12:19Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy traces to the checkout service, not to frontend-proxy. Deployment checkout in otel-demo rolled out at 2026-11-17T08:20:57Z to deployment revision 2 (new ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b), whose pod template changes KAFKA_ADDR from kafka:9092 to kafka:9999 with no other template difference. Kafka in this namespace listens on PLAINTEXT 9092 (plus controller 9093) and Service kafka exposes only ports 9092/9093, so the new checkout container repeatedly logs 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout' and exits with code 2; pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz is Running but not Ready (ContainersNotReady, restartCount 1, last and current termination reason Error/exitCode 2) and Service checkout has only a notReadyAddress. checkout span rate fell to 0 by 08:27:19Z. frontend's own error spans are confined to the checkout call path (POST /api/checkout, executing api route /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, tcp.connect), and frontend-proxy's ingress and 'router frontend egress' ERROR spans rose in lockstep from 0.0185/s at 08:21:19Z to a peak of 0.6778/s at 08:29:19Z against a 10-minute pre-onset baseline of 0.0123/s. Kafka itself and the other 9092-configured Kafka clients show no failure, so the Kafka-side and frontend-side hypotheses are rejected.

claims.text: For service frontend-proxy, span_name=ingress status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR rose from 0.0185/s at 2026-11-17T08:21:19Z to 0.1222/s at 08:22:19Z and peaked at 0.6778/s at 08:29:19Z, while ingress spans with STATUS_CODE_UNSET were 9.8-13.3/s; span_name 'router frontend egress' status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR shows the same pattern. The only status_code label values observed for frontend-proxy spans are STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

In service frontend, error-status spans were confined to POST, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and tcp.connect; each went from 0 at 2026-11-17T08:21:19Z to about 0.52-0.68/s by 08:25:19Z-08:29:19Z (aggregate frontend error-span rate 2.785/s at 08:29:19Z), while every other frontend operation in the same query returned 0.
Checkout stopped emitting spans: its all-operation span rate was 10.28/s at 2026-11-17T08:21:19Z, 5.02/s at 08:23:19Z, 3.01/s at 08:25:19Z and 0 from 08:27:19Z through 08:33:19Z.

Pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz (owner ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b) is Running but not Ready: condition Ready=False with reason ContainersNotReady since 2026-11-17T08:28:03Z, restartCount 1, lastState.terminated reason Error with exitCode 2 (started 08:20:59Z, finished 08:24:35Z) and current state terminated reason Error with exitCode 2 (started 08:24:36Z, finished 08:28:02Z).

Deployment checkout rolled out at 2026-11-17T08:20:57Z: it scaled new ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b from 0 to 1 at 08:20:57Z and old ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb from 1 to 0 at 08:21:00Z, killing pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9d9c8 at 08:21:00Z; checkout-849d65649b (revision 2) is the only ReplicaSet created in otel-demo after 07:55Z.

The old and new checkout pod templates differ in Kafka configuration: old ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb (revision 1) sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, new ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b (revision 2) sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999; both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout and otherwise identical env.

Kafka in otel-demo does not listen on 9999: pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh sets KAFKA_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093 with KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092; Service kafka (clusterIP 100.66.162.182) exposes only ports 9092 'plaintext' and 9093 'controller', and its Endpoints list only 9092 and 9093.

Logs of container checkout in pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz repeat 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout' and 'kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout' from 2026-11-17T08:21:29Z onward, and the process's own config dump records kafkaBrokerSvcAddr:kafka:9999.
Service checkout has no ready backends: its Endpoints object holds only notReadyAddresses 100.96.4.175 (targetRef Pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz) and no ready addresses on port 8080.

frontend and frontend-proxy themselves point at the expected upstreams: Deployment frontend sets CHECKOUT_ADDR=checkout:8080 and Deployment frontend-proxy sets FRONTEND_HOST=frontend, FRONTEND_PORT=8080; their pods frontend-675fd7b5c5-n4sbv and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-h7j7c are Running, Ready and have restartCount 0.

The fault originates in Deployment checkout in namespace otel-demo: its revision-2 pod template sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999, a port nothing listens on (Kafka listens and advertises 9092), so the pod logs i/o timeouts to kafka:9999 and exits with code 2 on every start, leaving no ready checkout endpoint, which is why frontend's checkout calls and frontend-proxy's checkout-path requests error.

Kafka pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and carries the standard 9092/9093 listener configuration, so the broker the incident dialed is up while not accepting port 9999.

Other Kafka clients still use kafka:9092 and show no incident-time error burst: Deployment accounting sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092 and Deployment fraud-detection sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, while their error-status span rates stayed at 0 (accounting) and about 0.0037/s background (fraud-detection) through 08:33:19Z.

A comparable pre-onset baseline exists inside the window: frontend-proxy error-status span rate measured over 10 minutes was 0.0123/s at 2026-11-17T08:10:00Z and 0.0123/s at 08:20:00Z, then 1.0/s at 08:30:00Z, while total frontend-proxy span rate stayed roughly flat (21.6/s, 22.3/s, 20.7/s).

Kafka is not the failing entity: its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, its Service exposes and its Endpoints list only 9092/9093, and the two other clients configured with kafka:9092 (accounting, fraud-detection) show no incident-time error burst; the only client dialing 9999 is the new checkout pod.

Neither frontend nor frontend-proxy is misconfigured or restarted: both pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, frontend targets checkout:8080 and frontend-proxy targets frontend:8080, and frontend's error spans are confined to the checkout operations while frontend-proxy's 'router frontend egress' errors mirror its ingress errors.

Rejected: a Kafka-side change or Kafka outage caused these failures. Kafka advertises and exposes 9092/9093 consistently, its pod is Ready with 0 restarts, other 9092 clients are unaffected, and the previous checkout ReplicaSet already used kafka:9092 while producing about 10 spans/s.

Rejected: frontend-proxy or frontend broke on its own (own fault, restart, or wrong upstream address). Their pods are Ready with 0 restarts, their env resolves to frontend:8080 and checkout:8080, and their error spans are limited to the checkout call path.

The revision-2 rollout that set KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999 appears to have been applied through Helm release 'otel-demo' (the Deployment and both ReplicaSets carry meta.helm.sh/release-name=otel-demo and release-namespace=otel-demo), but the actor and source change cannot be verified because change history is not integrated in this Run.

The falling frontend-proxy error rate from 08:31:19Z to 08:34:19Z (0.53/s to 0.18/s) is consistent with falling traffic rather than recovery: total ingress span rate dropped from 11.78/s at 08:29:19Z to 3.43/s at 08:34:19Z, so the error share stayed roughly near 5-6%.

Correct the checkout Deployment pod template so KAFKA_ADDR matches Kafka's listener (kafka:9092, as used by revision 1 and by accounting/fraud-detection), then confirm the replacement pod becomes Ready and Service checkout regains a ready endpoint.

After the checkout configuration is corrected, verify that frontend-proxy ingress/egress error spans return toward the 10-minute pre-onset background of 0.0123/s and that checkout span rate returns to about 10/s.

gaps: Alert rule definition unavailable: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for an unfiltered listing (both no_data), so how the annotation value 1.7333333333333332 was computed is unverified.

Alert start 2026-11-17T08:12:19Z precedes the earliest clear error deviation in span metrics (08:21:19Z-08:22:19Z); Prometheus series in this target begin near 2026-11-17T08:00:19Z, so pre-08:00Z error state and the alert's own onset are unknown rather than zero.

Jaeger data in this target ends at data_as_of 2026-11-17T08:09:46Z; a traces_search for service frontend-proxy over 08:10:00Z-08:36:09Z returned no_data and a frontend search over 08:20:00Z-08:36:09Z returned no_data, so no trace-level evidence covers the incident period.
The Kubernetes event listing covers only 2026-11-17T08:06:03Z-08:28:49Z, so events before and after that range are unknown.

Previous container instance logs for pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz were unavailable (kubelet reported no previous instance), and a filtered frontend pod log query for 08:15:00Z-08:36:09Z returned no_data, so application-log confirmation on the frontend side is missing.

The Kafka container log view (8e8f4e7b-335a-4344-8d73-bf62005e9dcf-t1) was marked incomplete (newest 40 of 1500 lines), so only the shown 08:29:00Z-08:29:17Z window was inspected and nothing older in that stream is known.
A query for NetworkPolicy objects in otel-demo returned an empty result set (no_data); that empty result is not evidence of absence, so network-policy causes can be neither confirmed nor excluded.

Several services (cart, currency, email, product-catalog, shipping, quote, ad, image-provider, load-generator) produced no error-status series in the error-rate query; their error state during the window is unknown rather than zero.
kube-state-metrics series (for example kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready) and http_*/rpc_* metric names returned no_data in this target, so only span-derived signals were available.
change_history is not integrated, so who or what applied Deployment checkout revision 2 cannot be verified.
next_steps: Diff the Helm release otel-demo values for checkout to confirm which change set KAFKA_ADDR to kafka:9999 and revert it to kafka:9092 (or, if 9999 is intended, add a matching Kafka listener and Service port, which the current Kafka pod and Service do not have).
Once checkout is Ready, watch frontend-proxy and frontend error-span rates for POST /api/checkout to confirm the alert clears.
Inspect the Prometheus/Alertmanager rule source for RequestErrorRate to reconcile its reported current value 1.7333333333333332 and start time with the observed error onset.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
